sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Yashpal Yadav,Sunil Kumar Yadav Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Vivek Varma,J.
Heard counsel for the applicants and Sri Vikas Sahai, learned A.G.A. for the State.

The present 482 Cr.P.C. application has been filed to quash the charge-sheet dated 25.8.2016 and proceedings of criminal case no. 1108 of 2016 (State vs. Ramavtar and others) arising out of case crime no. 55 of 2016, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P. Act, P.S. Deorania,
District Bareilly pending in the Court of Civil Judge (J.D.)/ Judicial Magistrate Baheri, District Bareilly.
Learned counsel for the applicants submits that the present dispute arises out of matrimonial discord between the applicant no. 1 and the opposite party no. 2.

sentences.text: It is also stated that compromise deed dated 13.12.2021 had been filed by the parties before the learned court below.

It is further stated that pursuant to the order dated 18.11.2022 passed by this Court in Application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. No. 11770 of 2017 (Ram Autar and another vs. State of U.P. and another) the parties appeared before the Court below and the learned court below has verified the aforesaid compromise vide order dated 30.11.2022.

entities.text: Cr.P.C. No. 11770 of 2017 (Ram Autar and another vs. State of U.P. and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The verification order of the court below is annexed as Annexure-7 to the affidavit.

In fact, it is submitted that if the criminal prosecution is allowed to proceed it may create further complication in the otherwise normal relationship that is arising between the hitherto bitterly estranged couple and their families.
The opposite party no. 2 had also appeared before the Court below and was identified by the learned counsel before the Court below.
He has not filed any affidavit in the present case before this Court disputing the aforesaid facts.

In view of the fact that the dispute appears to be purely of a personal nature being a matrimonial dispute that has been mutually settled between the parties, to their satisfaction, no useful purpose would be served in allowing such a prosecution to proceed any further.

Thus, in view of the well settled principles of law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2003(4) SCC 675 (B.S. Joshi Vs. State of Haryana) as well as the Judgement of the Apex Court reported in J.T., 2008(9) SC 192 (Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another),
the proceedings of the aforesaid case is hereby set aside.
